surfaces.part: cobbled yard ground surface (dark earth joints, river cobbles)
low dressed stone kerb rim with 2px south front face along the south edges

answer.evidence: This is a flat ground autotile drawn top-down, not a standing object. The cobbled yard is a large horizontal surface. The only vertical element is the kerb, whose south face is 2 rows tall (the pale kerb top and its darker front line, e.g. x=88 rows 20-23 and x=131 rows 34-38). That is under the 3-row front-face threshold. There is no receding side face and no ellipse or roof. The silhouette is irregular, with a grass hole in the middle and a small isolated cobble tile at the top right, which fits autotile pieces lying on grass. It reads as a flat slab with only a thin kerb lip on its south edge.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate has 15 visible tones per 16x16 tile against 7 for the paving reference and 3 for the grass reference, with 3% near-flat coverage, so it is at or above both references on density. Its dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline is tinted: dark earth-brown joints around the cobbles and a dark brown-grey beside the kerb stone, not a uniform black line. Each cobble is shaded individually, with a light top, a mid body and a dark joint, plus scattered grey stones and tonal variation, which gives about 5 steps on the cobble ramp. The kerb rim has a light top and a darker 2px south face. The grass around the patch has tufts and speckle comparable to the reference grass. Large areas of one flat colour are not visible. The overall structure is comparable to the references and does not look like a sticker.

answer.evidence: This is a flat ground autotile seen from above. The cobbled surface covers nearly the whole patch, with a pale 1-2 row kerb lip and a 2-row front face on the south edges. The column scan at x=44, 88 and 131 shows only 1-row light kerb lines and short dark joint runs, with no 3+ row vertical front face. The 2-row kerb face is below the 3-row minimum, so there is no real front face and the tile reads as a flat top-down slab.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate has 15 visible tones per 16x16 tile against 3 for the grass reference and 7 for the paving reference, so it is well above both. Near-flat coverage is 3%, with no large flat areas. The cobbles are shaded one by one (light, mid and dark warm browns, with grey stones mixed in) and sit in dark earth joints. The kerb rim has a light top, a mid face and a 2px dark front face on the south edge. Dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outlines lean brown and are tinted toward the neighbouring material, not black stickers. Grass tufts at the rim and the grass around the patch show some texture. The grass is slightly plainer than the cobbles but is comparable to the grass reference. The autotile edges and the inner hole read cleanly and match the reference kind.
